verdict: Ten-second read (cold, 1280x800 and 390x844, light, dark and reduced motion): 'a lesson on why two paints that match in the shop look different under the lamps at home; for anyone who has picked paint; first I would click Warm bulb or just watch the lamps change'. That read is right: the title, tagline and intro say it literally, and the first frame is one picture with the demo already running. One seamless taupe block (#A99488) splits into tan and rose at about 4 s and into sage and mauve at about 7.5 s. The first screen has 7 controls on desktop and 4 on the phone. The first 30 seconds succeed. The big blue Wiggle shows the whoa within 0.6 s: Fog's curve thrashes over a block that stays exactly rgb(169,148,136), while the 'was/now' swatches under the warm bulb drift 30 points apart. 'Make my own pair' reaches 'You made a metamer' in two drags, with a mouse and with touch. There are 0 console errors, the layout shift is about 0 and frames hold at 16.7 ms. What stands between this page and socks-off is mostly how legible the magic is, not correctness. The hero picture is beige on beige: the chips are only 1.6 to 2.0 times as bright as the wall. The bars for 'the three numbers your eye keeps' never visibly differ: 1 to 5 px of 62 even when the paints are 30 apart. The hero wiggle hides the WHY that figure 4 shows beautifully (the lamp's spikes behind the curve). On a phone the Wiggle button is 209 px below the fold. There are also two real bugs. The More panel's dimmer keeps describing the old lamp after another lamp is chosen. At the exact moment of success, the editor chart jumps 20 px under the finger. Fix the six S2 items and this is an 8.5 to 9. The science, the honest About panel, the exercises and explainer figures 3 to 5 are already at the level of the best explorable explanations.

findings.title: The 'three numbers your eye keeps' bars look identical under every lamp, even when the paints are 19 to 30 apart
findings.evidence:
Measured bar heights in px, each bar 62 px tall (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f017b37b-956c-5936-ade0-801c06b2aa0a/scratchpad/cameo/c2/qa2-first-impression/bars.mjs).
* Shop light, 0.0 apart: both chips 19.3/19.0/18.6.
* Warm bulb, 19.4 apart ('Clearly different'): Pebble L/M/S 21.1/21.2/18.1, Fog 18.1/17.0/19.1. The values behind them are 0.340/0.342/0.293 against 0.291/0.275/0.308.
* Daylight, 30.0 apart: Pebble 21.2/21.5/18.0, Fog 17.3/16.3/19.3.
So the largest visible difference is 5 px of 62, and every bar sits near 30% of its track. Screenshot under daylight: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f017b37b-956c-5936-ade0-801c06b2aa0a/scratchpad/cameo/c2/qa2-first-impression/bars-day.png. The chips are sage and mauve while the six bars look the same.
The page's core sentence is 'same three numbers, same color'. A newcomer comparing the bars sees the same numbers with different colors, which reads as the opposite lesson.
findings.fix:
1. Rescale the hero's bars (views.setBars) to a zoomed track from 0.15 to 0.45 of white, with a small break mark at the base. The warm-bulb gaps become L 10 px, M 14 px and S 3 px; under daylight they become 13, 17.5 and 4.4 px.
2. Draw the partner chip's height as a 2 px ink tick across each bar. Under the shop light the tick sits exactly on the bar top ('same three numbers'). Under other lamps the gap is obvious at a glance.
3. Put the three values (for example 0.340 · 0.342 · 0.293) in each bar group's aria-label and in a title tooltip.
4. Keep figure 3's full-scale bars as they are; there the full scale is the point.

findings.title: The hero wiggle shows motion without meaning: no lamp lines behind the big curve, and the consequence is a tiny swatch
findings.evidence:
During the wiggle the hero draws a white curve and a dashed ghost on a flat taupe block, with no axis and no lamp spectrum (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f017b37b-956c-5936-ade0-801c06b2aa0a/scratchpad/cameo/c2/qa2-first-impression/thirty/desk-wiggle-02200.png).
The same engine in figure 4 draws the lamp's spikes behind the curve. There you can SEE the curve swing freely where the lamp gives no light and stay close to the original near the 545 and 610 nm lines (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f017b37b-956c-5936-ade0-801c06b2aa0a/scratchpad/cameo/c2/qa2-first-impression/figs/fig4-wiggle-1500.png). But that figure is about 3,100 px further down.
The most striking evidence is the 'was/now' pair under the other lamp: dusty rose becomes sage, 30.6 apart. It is only about 180x70 px, tucked into the paper strip where Fog's curve was.
findings.fix:
1. In hero.js drawWiggleOverlay, before stroking the white curve, fill the current lamp's spectrum across Fog's block. Use figure 4's normalization and views.lampInk in light mode or the pale glow in dark mode, at about 30% opacity, as thin spikes or an area. Add a 10 px label 'the lamp's light' beside the tallest spike.
2. Promote the consequence: during the wiggle, show 'Under the warm bulb: was / now' as a full-width band along the bottom 56 px of Fog's block (two halves, live colors) instead of only inside the paper strip. The flicker then reads in the screenshot.
3. Keep the frozen block, the 'Color unchanged' badge and the one-line readouts exactly as they are.

findings.title: At the moment of success the editor chart jumps 20 px under the pointer mid-drag
findings.evidence:
One continuous drag tracked per pointermove (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f017b37b-956c-5936-ade0-801c06b2aa0a/scratchpad/cameo/c2/qa2-first-impression/editshift.mjs):
* Desktop: the editor canvas top is 494 px through step 14 (warm bulb 9.7). At step 15 (10.3, success) it moves to 514 px, and the next value leaps to 11.5.
* Phone 390x844: 457 to 477 px at 10.1, and the next value leaps to 12.5.
Cause: #goal swaps the 3-line goal for the 4-line (desktop) or 5-line (phone) success copy above the chart. The celebration lands as a glitch under the finger. Compare /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f017b37b-956c-5936-ade0-801c06b2aa0a/scratchpad/cameo/c2/qa2-first-impression/next3/desk-2-stroke1.png with /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f017b37b-956c-5936-ade0-801c06b2aa0a/scratchpad/cameo/c2/qa2-first-impression/next3/desk-2-stroke2.png.
findings.fix:
Reserve the goal's height for its longest variant. One way: make #goal a grid with every message variant stacked in one cell (grid-area 1/1), toggling visibility instead of textContent. Another: give .goal a min-height of 5lh on phones and 4lh on desktop, measured on the success copy.
Alternatively, move the success copy below the chart, next to #editor-status.
Re-run editshift.mjs: canvasTop must stay constant through the success step at 1280 and 390 px.

findings.title: The hero picture is beige on beige: the chips do not pop, and the first frame's dominant element is a flat taupe rectangle
findings.evidence:
Luminance contrast of the chips against the wall, sampled from the first frames (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user/f017b37b-956c-5936-ade0-801c06b2aa0a/scratchpad/cameo/c2/qa2-first-impression/cold/desk-light-t250.png, -t4800.png, -t8300.png):
* shop light 1.77:1;
* warm bulb 1.62:1 and 1.92:1;
* daylight 1.62:1 and 2.02:1.
The block is a 520x208 flat rectangle with a soft shadow, inside a tan gradient card with a dark pendant shade. The chips do not read as paint chips: there is no card edge, no printed name on the chip and no sheen.
Under the shop light there is no hint that two separate paints are there. When they split, the halves just change color, with no edge opening.
Next to Ciechanowski or Nicky Case it is tidy but quiet. A thumbnail or first glance does not stop the scroll.
findings.fix:
Keep every computed color. Change only the room and the chips:
1. Render the wall as a deeper paint through the same lamp pipeline (wall reflectance about 0.18 to 0.25), so it stays honest about the lamp's tint. Add a radial light pool under the lamp, centred on the chips, and a soft vignette. Target at least 3:1 between the chips and the wall edge.
2. Give each chip a paint-card identity: an off-white 6 to 8 px card border, the name in small caps printed on the card, and a faint top sheen (linear-gradient rgba(255,255,255,.06) to 0).
3. Make the match breaking literal: when the shown difference crosses 1, open a 3 px seam between the halves (200 ms, 0 under reduced motion), with a faint inner shadow. Close it again when they match.
Re-check the chips and text against the wall (contrast.mjs) and the colour-blind split after the change.

findings.title: The tagline and the intro's first sentence say the same thing back to back; 'Wiggle Fog' is cryptic as a button
findings.evidence: Tagline: 'Two paints match in the shop, then clash under the lamps at home. Here is why.' Intro, 40 px below: 'An interactive lesson on why two paints that match under one lamp can clash under another...'. The first ten seconds read the same idea twice. The primary button 'Wiggle Fog without changing its color' assumes the visitor already knows Fog has a curve.
findings.fix: Keep the intro, which the contract needs. Make the tagline carry the hook and the goal instead, for example: 'They matched on the paint-shop shelf. Under your lamps at home, they don't. Find the lamp that gives them away.' Label the button 'Wiggle Fog's curve (its color stays)', and keep 'Stop wiggling'.

praise: The first frame really is one picture with the phenomenon running: a seamless #A99488 block that splits into tan and dusty rose (19.4) and then sage and mauve (30.0) with no click. The cycle stops only on a deliberate hero action. Layout shift is about 0 and the crossfade and wiggle hold 16.7 ms frames (motion.mjs).

The wiggle is honest: Fog's block is recomputed from the moving curve every frame and stays exactly rgb(169,148,136), while the warm-bulb 'was/now' pair drifts 30 points apart. The one-line readouts ('Fog under the shop light: unchanged (0.0)' and 'Under the warm bulb: 30.6 from the original') never shift the layout.

'Make my own pair' is a real goal with instant feedback. The scene flips to the warm bulb and an inset proves the held shop-light match. Two natural drags reach 'You made a metamer of Pebble' on desktop and with touch, and the success copy stays true as you keep dragging.

The explainer figures are top-tier teaching: figure 3 (light from the paint times the three cone curves, with bar totals 0.312/0.306/0.300), figure 4 (the wiggle drawn over the lamp's spikes) and figure 5 (300 random pairs: 'the shop light split them more in 83 of every 100').
The exercises give specific, warm feedback on wrong answers ('Not quite. Under that lamp there is only one wavelength to send back: see step 5') and keep the numbers behind a disclosure.

Contract and robustness are clean. validate --contract is ok with 0 warnings. browser-check --contract is ok with 0 warnings, 0 console errors, 21 of 21 self-tests and 7 first-screen controls. There is no horizontal scroll from 320 to 1920 px, text contrast is at least 5.3:1 (scene text 11 to 14.5:1), focus rings are 3 px, and reduced motion gets 'Show another shape' instead of animation.
The About panel is a model of honesty: one plain sentence for the Opus cameo, 'what is computed and what is modeled', and dated, labelled sources with no vendors.
